title: Embedding quality benchmark runner and synthetic perturbation suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated, extensible benchmark runner that evaluates embedding accuracy and reranking quality across model variants and traffic slices. Key differentiators: (1) a synthetic perturbation generator that creates controlled signal/noise variations to test robustness, (2) a lightweight ranked-concordance scoring suite (nDCG/MRR/MAP) and embedding-stability fingerprints, and (3) nightly drift detection with statistical tests and alerting hooks. The runner should support offline batch runs against golden sets and scale to run continuous micro-benchmarks for high-traffic models.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can execute full evaluation for a single model variant end-to-end within a reproducible Docker image
Synthetic perturbation module can emit at least three perturbation classes: lexical noise, semantic paraphrase, and context-window truncation
Scoring artifacts include nDCG@5, MRR@10, cosine stability histograms, and per-query rank-change distributions
Nightly job produces a summarized report to the embeddings-dashboard and raises an alert when drift exceeds thresholds
Benchmarks include a latency/throughput profile for embedding+reranking pipeline under 1k, 5k, and 20k query batches
tasks: Design perturbation taxonomy and dataset subset selection (PM + Research)
Implement perturbation generator library with deterministic seeds
Build evaluation runner CLI and Dockerfile
Integrate scorer functions: nDCG, MRR, MAP, pairwise rank-change and stability fingerprinting
Create nightly orchestration in Airflow/Cron with artifact upload to S3 and dashboard sync
Add KS/AD statistical tests for embedding distance distributions and implement threshold config
Write alerting playbook and PagerDuty/Slack webhook integration
Run scaling tests and produce cost/time trade-off doc for continuous vs sample-based runs
updates: 2025-02-20: Ticket created after sync with PM and Research; scope agreed to include synthetic perturbations rather than only curated goldens.

2025-02-24: Spike completed — perturbation generator prototype (lexical/paraphrase) shows stable reproducibility with seed; prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/emb-eval-spike (PR #12)
2025-02-26: Design review with Research and Console teams. Decided to prioritize nDCG@5 and MRR@10 for early alerts. Console team requested an endpoint to pull per-model nightly CSVs.

2025-03-01: Implementation started for scorer module. Trade-off noted: computing full MAP across 1M-item gold sets is expensive; will use stratified sampling and micro-benchmarks for full-run windows.

2025-03-03: Added KS-test for cosine similarity distributions; initial thresholds suggested by Research (delta > 0.02 mean cosine) flagged several internal dev models — need to tune false positive rate. Created issue ENG-24012 to handle threshold tuning and false-positive suppression rules.
notes: Trade-offs: full-corpus daily runs are costly; choose hybrid strategy — nightly sampled runs (10k queries) + weekly full-run for top-customer models.
Alerting: use conservative thresholds initially and ship a 'silent' phase where alerts only create tickets for investigation before firing to PagerDuty.
Data retention: evaluation artifacts stored 90 days; raw gold sets versioned with model tags to ensure reproducibility.
Scaling: runner should support parallel shard execution across N workers; plan to reuse existing batching infra for throughput tests.
risks: High compute cost for frequent full-run evaluations; potential for noisy alerts if perturbations do not reflect production input distribution. Mitigations include stratified sampling, silent-alerting phase, and ongoing threshold calibration.
implementation_notes: Prefer numpy/FAISS for distance computations, avoid sleeping on GPU for scoring stage (CPU-bound).
Use deterministic seeds for all synthetic perturbations and document seed mapping for reproducibility.
Store evaluation artifacts as newline-delimited JSONL with schema version header.
